title: Modi Meets Iran's Pezeshkian at SCO Summit Amid US-Iran War
excerpt: The first face-to-face meeting between the two leaders since the outbreak of hostilities comes at a critical moment for regional stability and India's energy security.
body:
• PM Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan — their first in-person meeting since the US-Iran war began in February.
  • The SCO summit, marking the bloc's 25th anniversary, brought together around a dozen heads of state including Putin, Xi Jinping, and Pakistan's Shehbaz Sharif.
  • The meeting comes amid active hostilities near the Strait of Hormuz, with US forces striking Iranian positions and Iran retaliating with missile fire.
  • India has maintained diplomatic engagement with Iran through phone calls during the conflict while navigating its relationships with both Washington and Tehran.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan — the first face-to-face meeting between the two leaders since the war between the United States and Iran erupted in February.

The meeting, confirmed by both Indian and Iranian officials, took place against the backdrop of active hostilities in West Asia. On Sunday, US forces struck two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps rocket launcher positions on Larak Island after IRGC units were spotted preparing to launch rockets fitted with sea mines toward the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters. Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles targeting US forces in Jordan, though most incoming fire was intercepted.

A High-Stakes Diplomatic Moment

The bilateral came after several telephone conversations between Modi and Pezeshkian during the conflict. In their last call on June 30, Pezeshkian briefed Modi on developments in West Asia, while Modi reiterated the need for "continued efforts towards lasting peace and stability," according to India's Ministry of External Affairs.

"This meeting is very important and most of the leaders of the region will be present in it... this meeting is considered a symbol of the existence of diverse and independent voices in the global arena."

— Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran

Before departing for Bishkek, Pezeshkian said Iran does not seek war but "will respond with strength and determination to any aggression." He described instability in the region as "detrimental to all countries" and called for convergence on economic and security goals.

SCO Summit Context

The meeting took place within the broader framework of the 26th SCO summit, marking 25 years of the bloc that brings together Russia, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, four Central Asian nations, and Belarus. Around a dozen heads of state gathered in Bishkek, including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Putin and Xi have historically used SCO summits to project a unified front against Western influence. This year's gathering takes place amid multiple active conflicts — the ongoing Ukraine war, now in its fifth year, and the six-month US-Iran confrontation — along with trade wars driven by US tariffs on Chinese and Indian goods.

This month, the US imposed secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners across gold, technology, digital assets, aviation, and maritime transport. China, a major importer of Iranian oil, said it would "firmly defend" its interests. Iran, whose SCO membership dates to 2023, has sought to use the bloc to circumvent Western sanctions, though analysts say concrete benefits remain uncertain.

India's Balancing Act

For India, the Modi-Pezeshkian meeting highlights New Delhi's careful diplomatic balancing act. India has maintained engagement with Iran — a key energy and connectivity partner, particularly through the Chabahar port — while simultaneously deepening ties with the United States and managing the fallout of the conflict on global energy markets.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes, is a critical chokepoint for India's energy imports. Any sustained disruption would directly affect India's economy, already contending with elevated crude prices and a weakened rupee.

Modi also met Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan earlier on Monday and is expected to hold bilateral talks with Putin later in the day. A potential meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping was also anticipated, according to Livemint. India has been an SCO member since 2017.

What to Watch

The substance of the Modi-Pezeshkian discussion has not been publicly disclosed, but the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and its implications for energy security are likely to have featured, according to NDTV. The meeting signals India's continued effort to maintain diplomatic channels with all parties in the West Asian conflict — a stance that has implications for energy prices, remittance flows from the Gulf, and the safety of millions of Indians working in the region.
